description:
FILED s450t (Opus, agent T of round 8), probed while finishing #561.
PRE-EXISTING.

perlvar: %+ maps a capture NAME to its (last) captured string, %- maps it to
an ARRAY REF of every capture with that name, in group order.

PROBE (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL at s450t):
    'X' =~ /(?<X>X)/;
    print "plus=[", $+{X}, "] minus=[", (ref($-{X}) || $-{X}), "]\n";
    print "elem=[", (ref($-{X}) eq 'ARRAY' ? $-{X}[0] : 'NOTARRAY'), "]\n";
  perl: plus=[X] minus=[ARRAY]   elem=[X]
  PCL:  plus=[X] minus=[X]       elem=[NOTARRAY]

So %- is currently a SECOND COPY of %+ rather than the array-of-captures
hash.  The runtime builds both in set-match-vars (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp); the
fix is per-name accumulation into an adjustable vector wrapped as an array
ref, with the SAME ordering rule as the group numbering.

NOTE the interaction: %{^CAPTURE_ALL} is mapped onto %- by the emitter
(task #412), so this fixes both spellings at once.

BAR: the probe above, plus a duplicate-name pattern
`"ab" =~ /(?<n>a)(?<n>b)/` (perl needs `use re 'eval'`-free branch reset or
two identical names -- probe the exact legal spelling first), and a row in
an existing regex guard file.
subject: %- values must be ARRAYREFS of every capture for that name; PCL stores the string, so `$-{X}` is "X" where perl gives ARRAY(0x..)
